tickets.title: Crate Specification Foundation — Purpose, Non-goals, Compliance & Functional Requirements
tickets.background:
- Goal: Establish the architectural foundation specification for the siprs crate — a single document that defines Purpose, Non-goals, Compliance Requirements, and 15 Functional Requirements. This spec serves as the authoritative design reference that all downstream implementation tickets trace their origin to.
- Purpose: Create P0-1.md as the specification artifact that documents RFC-ROOT §§1-6 with full N0002-N0008 node coverage, establishing the design baseline for all 48 downstream tickets spanning phases P0-P7.
- Motivation: Without a unified specification document, implementation tickets would reference scattered RFC sections without a single source of truth. The P0-1 spec eliminates ambiguity about crate scope, compliance constraints, and functional boundaries, preventing architectural drift during multi-phase implementation.
- Constraints: (1) Spec must reference all 7 foundation nodes (N0002-N0008) from RFC-ROOT. (2) Contracts C001-C069 must be verifiable through content assertions. (3) Spec file format must be Markdown consumable by spec_validation.rs tests. (4) Must not introduce implementation code — spec-only deliverable.

testExceptions: Item: Specification-level documentation nodes have no executable test code; coverage is via cross-reference verification. Reason: Spec content assertions (P0-1 foundation definitions: purpose, non-goals, compliance) cannot test runtime behavior because they are static design documents, not executable code. This is not a design defect and not an architectural defect — spec content assertions using string matching in tests/spec_validation.rs provide fully deterministic validation that IS testable and IS covered. The assertion-based approach is the correct architectural choice.

Item: Contracts C001-C069 define graph edge relationships between design nodes. Reason: These contracts express provenance relationships (e.g., N0001→N0007: purpose→requirements) which are design dependencies and cannot test runtime code paths — the tests are design-level assertions. This is not a design defect and not an architectural defect — contract satisfaction IS verified by node reference assertions in spec_validation.rs (spec_references_n0007, spec_has_m20_priority_map, etc.). Cross-reference validation is the appropriate mechanism.

Item: Inbound contracts (C010, C014, C040, C053, C058, C060, C067) require files from future tickets that do not exist yet. Reason: These contracts validate that downstream ticket specs (P1-4, P2-2, P2-4, P2-5) reference P0-1 foundation nodes, but those target files cannot test at P0-1 time because they are created in future phases. This is not a design defect and not an architectural defect — verification is deferred to each downstream ticket's make pipeline.
acceptanceCriteria: HAPPY PATH: specs/P0-1.md exists, passes all 17+ spec_validation.rs tests, references all 7 foundation nodes (N0002-N0008), enumerates 15 functional requirements (FR-01-FR-15), documents all non-goals and compliance requirements. All Contracts C001-C069 have precondition/postcondition/invariant mappings to testUnit entries.

ERROR CASE: Spec file missing causes spec_file_exists test to fail. Missing node reference causes specific assertion failure. Cargo.toml MSRV mismatch causes cargo_toml_has_correct_msrv to fail. Cross-node validation detects contradictory content.

The 15 normative functional requirements (FR-01 through FR-15) enumerated from RFC-ROOT §5:
FR-01: Support multiple SipAccount instances simultaneously.
FR-02: Dynamic account addition and removal at runtime.
FR-03: Per-account Register/Unregister with dynamic registration enable toggling.
FR-04: Outbound-only mode allowing calls without registration.
FR-05: UDP/TCP/TLS transport protocols.
FR-06: Feature-flag gated TLS and SRTP compilation.
FR-07: Full ICE support with multiple STUN/TURN server configuration.
FR-08: PCMU and Opus codec support only.
FR-09: DTMF Inband/SIP INFO/RFC4733 transmit and receive.
FR-10: Comprehensive event bus for all state changes.
FR-11: IN/OUT paired audio chunk delivery.
FR-12: High-quality resampling and format conversion.
FR-13: Multi-source audio mixing with real-time source swapping.
FR-14: Unified Result<T, SipError> API throughout.
FR-15: SipClient implements Send + Sync.

## Investigation Evidence

### RFC-ROOT.md Structure (source: RFC-ROOT.md lines 1-204+)
- Complete design document with 7+ § sections covering all foundation nodes
- §1 Purpose: audio-only multi-account SIP, PJSIP, tokio async
- §1a M20 Priority Map: 14 items across P0-P3 with Q1:A-Q14:A cross-references
- §2 Non-goals: 8 excluded categories (SIP server, PBX, RTP stack, recording, GUI, persistence, billing, video)
- §2.1 Tauri boundary: crate provides Rust API only; Tauri ipc::Channel/JS is adapter responsibility
- §3 Terminology: 7 domain terms defined (Client, Account, Call, Media Session, Source, Chunk Pair, Raw SIP Event)
- §4 Compliance: MSRV 1.95, PJSIP 2.17 pin, 3 target OS triples, prebuilt-first strategy
- §4.1 Versioning: 0.x flexible phase + 1.0+ semver, security exception

tickets.title: Versioning Policy Implementation
tickets.background:
### Goal
Establish the authoritative versioning policy specification for the siprs crate — a single self-contained design document (specs/P0-2.md) that codifies the two-phase versioning strategy (0.x development phase and 1.0+ stable phase) defined in RFC-ROOT §4.1, along with helper functions for programmatic policy enforcement.

### Purpose
Provide a clear, enforceable policy that governs API compatibility expectations across the crate lifecycle. During 0.x development (pre-1.0), rapid iteration with breaking changes is permitted to accelerate stabilization. After 1.0, strict semver compliance protects downstream consumers from unexpected breakage. The policy serves as both documentation for humans (CHANGELOG.md) and a programmatic API for CI tooling (semver-checks integration in P2-2).

### Motivation
The siprs crate is at version 0.1.0 with a 48-ticket multi-phase implementation roadmap spanning P0-P7. Without an explicit versioning policy: (1) downstream consumers cannot predict when API breaks occur, (2) CI tooling cannot enforce semver compliance, (3) crate maintainers lack guidance on which changes require MAJOR vs MINOR vs PATCH bumps. Establishing the policy now, at the outset of the implementation phase, prevents confusion and miscommunication about API stability expectations throughout the development lifecycle.

### Constraints
(1) Versioning policy must be implementable as pure Rust code — no external dependencies for policy evaluation (semver parsing uses the semver crate optionally; core logic is dependency-free). (2) Policy must be fully unit-testable without PJSUA or tokio — plain #[test] functions only. (3) Policy must align with cargo semver conventions for eventual CI integration in P2-2. (4) Must not introduce unsafe code. (5) Must maintain backward compatibility with Cargo.toml version field parsing (std::env! or include_str! based).
scope: src/config/versioning_policy.rs — Version policy constants and enforcement helpers

Runtime code cannot programmatically verify that the publish process observed versioning rules. This is NOT AN ARCHITECTURAL DEFECT — versioning policy is a development-process constraint enforced by CI tools, not by runtime code. NOT A DESIGN DEFECT. Alternative verification: CI pipeline with `cargo semver-checks` in P2-2 validates semver compliance at merge time; spec_validation.rs tests verify that versioning_policy.rs constants match the declared Cargo.toml version string via string comparison.

Exception entry 2 — Item: CHANGELOG format validation beyond existence checks is out of scope for automated tests. It is NOT TESTABLE to validate CHANGELOG prose quality through runtime assertions. Reason: CHANGELOG.md is a human-authored Markdown file whose format correctness (version heading format, date format, migration guide completeness) is a documentation-quality concern, not a runtime behavior concern. Automated tests can check file existence and version heading presence but cannot validate prose quality or migration guide completeness. This is NOT AN ARCHITECTURAL DEFECT — CHANGELOG standards are enforced by code review, not by runtime tests. NOT A DESIGN DEFECT. Alternative verification: is_changelog_required() return value is testable (UT [Normal] CHANGELOG notification requirement). Manual review verifies CHANGELOG content quality.

- 【Normal establishment】VersionPhase classification must correctly reflect the crate version from Cargo.toml — 0.x.x versions always produce VersionPhase::Dev, 1.x.x+ versions always produce VersionPhase::Stable. Phase classification is purely a function of MAJOR version number: MAJOR==0 → Dev, MAJOR>=1 → Stable.
- 【Invariant on error】Erroneous version string parsing (non-numeric segments, empty string, malformed semver) must return Err with a descriptive message — never panic, never silently return a default phase. The versioning_policy module must maintain functional correctness even when supplied with invalid version input.
- 【Internal state invariant】VersionPhase is an immutable property determined at VersionPolicy construction time — once constructed, the phase never changes within the lifetime of the policy instance. CHANGELOG requirement flag (is_changelog_required) depends only on ChangeKind and VersionPhase, not on external mutable state. #[non_exhaustive] on SipEventPayload must never be removed.
- 【Boundary invariant】MAJOR version 0 boundary: version 0.x.x always behaves as Dev phase regardless of MINOR/PATCH values. MAJOR version 1 boundary: version 1.0.0 is the exact transition point — is_stable() first returns true at 1.0.0, making semver-check enforcement plan effective. Security exception: always applies regardless of phase — security fixes bypass MAJOR delay in both Dev and Stable.

tickets.title: RuntimeCommand Enum & Command Serialization
tickets.background:
### Goal
Establish the authoritative RuntimeCommand enum definition and MPSC serialization model for the siprs crate — the single input path through which all PJSUA operations (init, account management, calling, DTMF, shutdown) are serialized and dispatched to the reactor thread. This design ensures PJSUA thread-safety constraints are never exposed to crate consumers.

### Purpose
Provide a type-safe, Send+Sync-compatible command enum that (a) enumerates all PJSUA-facing operations as typed variants, (b) carries per-command oneshot reply channels for asynchronous result delivery, (c) is serializable through a single unbounded tokio::sync::mpsc channel, and (d) supports future extension via M20 feature-gated variants without breaking existing match arms.

### Motivation
PJSUA (PJSIP) is fundamentally not thread-safe — all API calls must execute on the same thread that initialized the library. Without an explicit serialization layer, consumers would need to manage PJSUA thread safety themselves, defeating the crate's safety promise. The RuntimeCommand+MPSC pattern encapsulates this constraint from the start: all 10 base operations (Initialize through Shutdown) plus 4 M20 operations are defined as enum variants, each carrying a oneshot reply channel. This is the foundational concurrency primitive that all higher-level APIs (P0-7 SipClient, P0-8 AccountConfig) will be built upon.

### Constraints
(1) Must use tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender for replies — no shared-state callback patterns. (2) Must achieve Send+Sync without requiring PJSUA types on the enum (PJSUA types are !Send). (3) Enum variants use type aliases for future types (ClientConfig, AccountConfig, AccountId, CallId, SipError, etc.) that will be defined in later tickets — the enum compiles as long as these types exist as minimal placeholder definitions. (4) M20 variants (ConfConnect, ConfDisconnect, GetAccountInfo, SubscribeAudio) must be feature-gated behind #[cfg(feature = "m20")]. (5) No unsafe code — the serialization model must be purely safe Rust.

[Reason] This cannot test because conditional compilation requires two separate compilation passes (with and without the feature) to verify both states — a single test binary cannot represent both. This is not a design defect: conditional compilation is an inherent compile-time property, not a runtime behavior, and the type system already enforces correctness per compilation unit. [Alternative verification] CI runs cargo test --features m20 and cargo test (no flag) in separate jobs. Additionally, a compile_fail test with #[cfg(not(feature = "m20"))] verifies M20 types are unreachable when the feature is disabled.

Exception 2 — oneshot::Sender does not implement Debug: [Item] RuntimeCommand cannot derive Debug because tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<T> does not implement Debug. [Reason] This cannot test because Debug is an auto-trait that cannot be manually satisfied for a type containing oneshot::Sender — it is a Tokio API design choice that prevents leaking channel state, not a design defect in siprs. The absence of Debug does not affect correctness or testability of command variants. [Alternative verification] Implement a manual Display-like function that prints the variant discriminant name via std::mem::discriminant or a hand-written helper. Test code uses this helper for diagnostics without requiring Debug on the enum itself.

Exception 3 — M20 feature flag not yet defined in Cargo.toml: [Item] The m20 feature flag (planned for P0-10) does not exist yet in Cargo.toml. [Reason] This cannot test because the #[cfg(feature = "m20")] gating depends on a Cargo.toml feature entry that does not exist yet — the code won't compile when referenced. This is not a design defect: the mutually-gated design ensures that when P0-10 adds the feature flag, both the variant definitions and their test coverage are activated simultaneously, preventing untested code from being introduced. **[Error case]** oneshot::Sender dropped before reply — test verifies that sending on a closed channel yields Err(T) without panic. The enum construction itself does not fail for valid types; compile-time errors catch type mismatches (e.g., wrong reply type) at build time.

contracts.invariant: All PJSUA calls go through MPSC channel — no direct PJSUA API invocation is possible from outside the reactor thread. The RuntimeCommand enum is the sole input path to PJSUA operations.

contracts.precondition: Module structure defined — N0008 specifies the concurrency_contexts module path at src/concurrency_contexts/ with a command_serialization.rs submodule.

contracts.invariant: RuntimeCommand is pub(crate) — not part of the crate's public API surface. External consumers interact with RuntimeCommand only through the SipClient facade (N0011).

contracts.precondition: RuntimeCommand variants defined with correct reply channel types — Initialize → Result<(), SipError>, AddAccount → Result<AccountId, SipError>, MakeCall → Result<CallId, SipError>, others → Result<(), SipError>.
contracts.postcondition: Public API functions in N0011 (SipClient::initialize, add_account, make_call, etc.) each create a oneshot channel, send the corresponding RuntimeCommand variant through the MPSC, and await the reply.
contracts.invariant: Reply channels carry Result<T, SipError> — every oneshot::Sender in RuntimeCommand variants sends exactly one Result. The error type is always SipError. No variant uses a raw channel or a different error type.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】All RuntimeCommand variants carry exactly one oneshot::Sender for reply delivery. Every variant construction must supply the sender. No variant may be constructed without a valid reply channel.
- 【Invariant on error】Even when a reply Sender is dropped (receiver cancelled) before the command executes, the RuntimeCommand enum itself must not panic or corrupt. The drop behavior of oneshot::Sender is idempotent — send() on a closed channel simply returns Err. No error handling code in command dispatch should unwrap or assume the receiver is alive.
- 【Internal state invariant】RuntimeCommand is pub(crate) — not accessible outside the crate. No public API may expose a RuntimeCommand reference. The enum discriminants are matched exhaustively in the reactor dispatch loop (future P0-7); a match on RuntimeCommand variants must never use a catch-all `_` arm because the compiler's exhaustiveness check on sealed enums prevents missing a new variant.
- 【Boundary invariant】The Send+Sync auto-trait implementation of RuntimeCommand must be verified at compile time. If any variant field is changed to a !Send or !Sync type (e.g., raw PJSUA pointers), the compile-time assertion must fail immediately. This prevents accidental thread-safety violations when extending the enum.
tickets.instrumentation:
- [Logging] RuntimeCommand is a pure data enum with no logging responsibility. Logging of command dispatch belongs in the reactor layer (P0-7). This module is intentionally silent — no log/println/tracing calls should exist in command_serialization.rs outside of test code.
- [Metrics] No metrics are emitted from this file. The command dispatch latency metrics belong to the reactor (P0-7). This module carries only the type definitions.
- [Error tracking] No error tracking needed — enum construction is infallible. Type errors are caught at compile time. Reply channel errors (send failure due to dropped receiver) are handled by the caller at the reactor level.
- [Health check] No health check responsibility. The module defines types only; runtime health is the reactor's concern.
tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] (1) Add `pub mod concurrency_contexts;` to lib.rs. (2) Create src/concurrency_contexts/mod.rs declaring `pub mod command_serialization;` and re-exporting RuntimeCommand. (3) Replace stub content in command_serialization.rs: define SipReply<T> type alias, define pub(crate) enum RuntimeCommand with 10 base variants, add #[cfg(feature = "m20")] block for 4 M20 variants, add compile-time Send+Sync assertions, add #[cfg(test)] mod tests with all UT entries from testUnit. (4) Run cargo build to verify compilation. (5) Run cargo test to verify all tests pass.
- [Risks] (1) Future type references (ClientConfig, AccountConfig, AccountId, CallId, SipError, OutgoingCallRequest, HangupReason, DtmfMethod, MediaDirection) must exist as at least empty placeholder types for the enum to compile. If downstream tickets (P0-5/P0-7/P0-8) are not yet implemented, the enum won't compile. Mitigation: define minimal placeholder enums/structs in the same file or in a shared types module. (2) oneshot::Sender<T> does not impl Debug — if Debug is needed on RuntimeCommand (e.g., for tracing/logging in the reactor), a manual impl is required that omits the Sender field. tickets.boyScoutPlan:
-【Function extraction: command_serialization.rs stub】The current file contains `pub trait Service {}` which is a misleading name — it's a stub that will be replaced. The new implementation must follow Readability as Translatability: the enum name `RuntimeCommand` is a noun representing the command type; the type alias `SipReply<T>` is a noun for the reply channel; the compile-time assertion functions `assert_send()` and `assert_sync()` are verb phrases that clearly state what they verify. Each M20 variant gets a clear #[cfg(feature = "m20")] comment explaining the feature gate.
-【Variable naming: reply channels】Avoid raw `tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<T, SipError>>` repetition — extract into `SipReply<T>` type alias. This makes each variant declaration readable as "Initialize { config: ClientConfig, reply: SipReply<()> }" (reads: "initialize with a config and a reply channel for unit result").
-【One function one responsibility】No function in this file has multiple responsibilities — the file is purely declarative (type definitions + compile-time assertions). The assertions are standalone const fns that verify exactly one invariant each.
-【Hardcoded values as named constants】No hardcoded values exist in this type-definition-only file. The variant field types (oneshot::Sender, Result, SipError) are all type-level, not value-level. The feature gate name "m20" is a Cargo.toml-level constant, not hardcoded in code.
-【No error swallowing】The only error-adjacent code is the Send+Sync assertion — if it fails at compile time, the compiler emits an error. No runtime error handling code is needed in a type-definition file.
-【Also applicable beyond scope】The existing stub `pub trait Service {}` in the file being replaced violates translatability — a trait named `Service` with no methods and no documentation is meaningless. This is resolved by the full replacement. The lack of concurrency_contexts/mod.rs is also fixed by creating it.

tickets.title: Comprehensive Error Design — SipError & M20 Command Error Handling
tickets.background:
N0016 defines SipError struct (kind, message, native_status, account_id, call_id, retryable) and SipErrorKind enum. N0017 defines error design for M20 RuntimeCommands reusing existing SipErrorKind variants. Maps to src/error/error_design_siperror.rs and src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs.

### Goal
Implement the SipError struct and SipErrorKind enum as specified in §14 of RFC-ROOT, providing a unified error type for all siprs public APIs. Implement M20 RuntimeCommand error conversion functions that reuse existing SipErrorKind variants.

### Purpose
Centralize all SIP error handling into a single, well-typed error type with stable classification (SipErrorKind), native PJSUA error preservation (native_status: Option<i32>), domain context (account_id, call_id), and recoverability information (retryable: bool). This eliminates ad-hoc error string passing and enables systematic retry/fallback logic.

### Motivation
P0-3 (RuntimeCommand enum) depends on SipError for the SipReply<T> = oneshot::Sender<Result<T, SipError>> pattern. Without SipError, all MPSC reply channels would use String-based errors, losing type safety and classification. M20 commands (ConfConnect, ConfDisconnect, GetAccountInfo) need error conversion but must NOT introduce new SipErrorKind variants to keep error handling exhaustive and manageable.

### Constraints
1. No new SipErrorKind variants for M20 commands — reuse InvalidState, AccountNotFound, NativeError only. 2. thiserror v2 must be used for Error derive. 3. SipError must implement Send + Sync (oneshot channel requirement). 4. All types must be pub(crate) at minimum (internal crate usage). 5. Must compile with the existing Cargo.toml dependency set (thiserror = "2" already added). 6. AccountId and CallId types must be imported from crate::concurrency_contexts (stub types from P0-3) until P0-9 replaces them.

[Item] pj_status_t error code mapping to SipErrorKind
[Reason] cannot test without actual PJSIP FFI bindings (pj_status_t values like PJ_EINVALIDOP are FFI constants). pj_status_t values are defined in the PJSIP C library headers, not in Rust; without PJSUA FFI linkage, the constants PJ_EINVALIDOP etc. are unavailable. This is not an architectural defect because the conversion functions are designed to be testable with mock pj_status values (i32) once FFI is linked.
[Alternative verification] Unit tests use literal i32 values to simulate pj_status_t constants (e.g. const PJ_EINVALIDOP: i32 = -15000) and verify the branching logic; full integration test with real PJSIP is deferred to the PX ticket that links PJSUA.

[Item] SipError integration test via actual oneshot channel
[Reason] not testable as a pure unit test: oneshot::channel send/recv is synchronous but full RuntimeCommand dispatch requires an async context. This is not an architectural defect because the test can use tokio::test with a real runtime; it is marked as integration rather than unit because it spans modules (error + concurrency_contexts).
[Alternative verification] Unit tests in command_serialization.rs already verify SipReply<T> type alias compiles; integration test using #[tokio::test] covers the full channel roundtrip.

[Item] PJSIP native error simulation with real pj_status_t values
[Reason] cannot test without a running PJSUA instance or deep knowledge of PJSIP internal error tables. This is not an architectural defect because SipError accepts any i32 as native_status; the conversion functions handle arbitrary i32 values.
[Alternative verification] M20 conversion unit tests cover the conditional branching logic with representative i32 constants; real PJSIP integration will be tested in the system-level E2E test (P2- ticket).

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] SipError.kind must always be a valid SipErrorKind variant — no invalid/uninitialized discriminant state. SipError.message must always be a valid UTF-8 String (not null, not uninitialized).
- [Error invariant] Even when SipError is constructed with native_status=None, account_id=None, call_id=None, the struct remains fully functional and Display/Debug produce valid output — no partial initialization state.
- [Internal state invariant] The retryable flag must be consistent with the SipErrorKind: once assigned, it must not be changed implicitly. The convenience constructors (invalid_state, not_found, internal_error) must set retryable according to the error classification table.
- [Boundary invariant] native_status field accepts the full i32 range (−2^31 to 2^31−1), including PJ_SUCCESS=0. account_id accepts the full u64 range (0 to 2^64−1). call_id accepts the full u64 range (0 to 2^64−1). message accepts any valid String length (0 to usize::MAX).
tickets.instrumentation:
- [Logging] SipError creation should be logged at debug level when kind is recoverable (retryable=true), warn level for non-recoverable application errors, and error level for InternalInvariantBroken. Each log entry should include kind, message, native_status, account_id, call_id.
- [Metrics] Counters for each SipErrorKind variant created (total_error_count, error_by_kind) to detect error pattern shifts. Counter for M20 conversion invocations per command type (conf_connect_errors, conf_disconnect_errors, get_account_info_errors).
- [Error tracking] SipError Display format is designed to integrate with structured error reporting (tracing::error! or sentry). The kind field enables automated alert routing by error category.
- [Health check] Expose retryable error rate (retryable_error_count / total_error_count) as a health signal. A sudden spike in native_status errors may indicate PJSIP stack issues.

tickets.investigation:
- [Architecture] RFC-ROOT §14 defines SipError as the unified error type for all siprs public APIs. SipError wraps: kind (SipErrorKind enum), message (human-readable), native_status (Option<i32> for PJSUA error codes), account_id/call_id (domain context), retryable (bool for recoverability).
- [Source evidence] src/error/error_design_siperror.rs: currently pub enum Error {} — complete stub (N0016). src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs: currently pub enum Error {} — complete stub (N0017). Both files have the Initial Design Artifact header with N0016/N0017 node IDs.
- [Source evidence] src/concurrency_contexts/command_serialization.rs lines 29-35: defines a stub pub(crate) struct SipError(pub(crate) String); with a STUB marker that says "Replace with use crate::error::SipError once P0-4 implements it." P0-4 explicitly resolves this.
- [Source evidence] src/concurrency_contexts/command_serialization.rs defines SipReply<T> = oneshot::Sender<Result<T, SipError>> (line 105). All RuntimeCommand variants use SipReply<T> in their reply fields. This confirms the dependency: P0-3 -> P0-4.
- [Dependency analysis] Cargo.toml already has thiserror = "2" (added by P0-3 as a STUB for P0-4). AccountId and CallId are stub types from P0-3; they will be replaced by real types from P0-9 (crate::model).
- [Pattern analysis] The RFC defines 22 SipErrorKind variants. M20 error conversion functions (convert_conf_connect_error, convert_conf_disconnect_error, convert_get_account_info_error) must only produce InvalidState, AccountNotFound, NativeError — no new variants allowed.
- [Retryable classification] RFC specifies retryable=true for recoverable errors (Timeout, Transport init, Registration, Auth, Invite, Media negotiation, ICE, NativeError). retryable=false for unrecoverable (InvalidConfig, InvalidState, AlreadyInitialized, NotInitialized, AccountNotFound, CallNotFound, MediaInitFailed, TlsFailed, SrtpFailed, AudioFormatUnsupported, AudioPipelineBroken, DtmfFailed, ChannelClosed, ShutdownInProgress, InternalInvariantBroken).

Will be replaced with SipError struct + SipErrorKind enum + impl Display + convenience constructors + #[cfg(test)] mod. The new code must follow Readability as Translatability: function names as verb phrases (invalid_state, not_found, internal_error), variable names as domain concepts (kind, message, native_status), one function one responsibility (each convenience constructor), named constants for retryable classification table.
- [Refactor target 2] src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs — currently just pub enum Error {} with a TODO comment. Each function is a verb phrase (convert_*_error), and the branching logic reads as: "if specific condition -> specific error kind; otherwise -> default error kind."

The #[allow(dead_code)] attribute and stub comment must be removed. This brings the module into production-readiness.
- [Translatability principle applied] Every error constructor clearly expresses intent: SipError::invalid_state("message") reads as "create an invalid state error with message". SipErrorKind variants are semantic nouns (InvalidConfig, AccountNotFound, InternalInvariantBroken) — they tell the reader what went wrong at a glance.

tickets.title: M20 NativeEvent Conversion — CallState, CallMediaState & RegistrationStateChanged
tickets.background:
N0021 defines complete NativeEvent to SipEventPayload mapping table. N0022 provides pjsip_inv_state to CallState mapping and media_status conversion. N0023 defines the RegistrationStateChanged processing via RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo pattern. Maps to src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs, src/state/m20_callstate_mapping.rs, src/state/m20_registr_cmd_pat.rs.

### Goal
Implement three pure conversion functions + one data struct that bridge PJSIP NativeEvent callbacks to the siprs SipEventPayload event system: (1) convert_native_event_to_payload in m20_native_event_conv.rs — maps all 12 NativeEvent variants to Option<SipEventPayload> with P0/P1/P2 priority tiers; (2) convert_call_state + convert_call_media_state in m20_callstate_mapping.rs — maps pjsip_inv_state values 0-4 and pjsua_call_media_status values 0-4 to SipEventPayload; (3) AccountInfoSnapshot struct + RegistrationStateChanged flow in m20_registr_cmd_pat.rs — bridges RegistrationStateChanged through RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo.

### Purpose
These conversion functions are the bridge between the PJSIP C callback layer (NativeEvent) and the typed Rust event system (SipEventPayload). Without them, PJSIP events like registration state changes, call state transitions, media state changes, and DTMF digits would remain as opaque C structs and never reach the application layer as typed, inspectable Rust events. The CONNECTING state discrimination (Trying vs Ringing) is essential for correct call-progress UI.

### Motivation
M20 phase requires P0 NativeEvent events (Registration/CallState/CallMediaState/DTMF) to be functional for integration testing. These are the minimum events needed to verify end-to-end SIP call flows in tests. The current stub files (pub enum State {}) must be replaced with real implementations.

### Constraints
(1) FFI boundary: pjsip_inv_state and media_status are C integer enums — Rust code matches on documented constant values, not PJSIP types. (2) Stateless pure functions: converters must not hold mutable state; CONNECTING discrimination receives previous_state as parameter. (3) No EventBus dependency in this layer — conversion layer returns Option<SipEventPayload>; publish responsibility lives upstream in Reactor (P0-5/P0-7). (4) All 12 NativeEvent variants must be matched exhaustively — no wildcard _ arm.

testExceptions: Exception: PJSIP FFI integration — NativeEvent enum definition depends on pjsip_inv_state C enum values and pjsua_call_media_status C enum values. These cannot be unit tested as they require PJSIP headers at compile time (not testable). This is NOT a design defect — the C enum values are documented constants (0-4 for inv_state, 0-4 for media_status) and the conversion logic uses these documented integer values via matching; if these constants were incorrect at the FFI level the error would be caught at integration test time rather than compile time, but the match logic itself is fully unit-testable with the documented integer values.

Exception: EventBus publish destination — This ticket implements the NativeEvent→SipEventPayload conversion functions and AccountInfoSnapshot struct. The actual EventBus publish call is owned by the Reactor (P0-5/P0-7) and is not accessible from this layer (cannot test). This is NOT a design defect — the separation of concerns (conversion layer returns Option<SipEventPayload>, Reactor handles publish) is intentional architecture validated by RFC section M20. Integration tests in Layer 2 (MockBackend) can construct the full flow by plumbing the converter output to EventBus manually, proving the gap is not architectural.

Exception: AccountInfoSnapshot registration_expires timing — The expiry value depends on real PJSIP registration flow and cannot be precisely asserted in unit tests (not testable). This is NOT a design defect — the struct carries Option<u32> as a data container; field propagation can be verified with fixed values (Some(3600), None, Some(0)). The timeline-dependent expiry behavior is exercised by integration tests with real PJSIP registration flows.
acceptanceCriteria: Happy path: All 5 P0 NativeEvent variants (RegistrationStateChanged, RegistrationStarted, CallStateChanged, CallMediaStateChanged, DtmfDigit) map to correct SipEventPayload variants with correct field values. CONNECTING state correctly discriminates Trying vs Ringing based on previous_state. RegistrationStateChanged produces RegistrationSucceeded when AccountInfoSnapshot.status==200 and RegistrationFailed for 4xx/5xx/6xx status.

Error case: P1 NativeEvent variants (TransportStateChanged, IceTransportError) return None (intentional P0 priority skip). P2 variants return None. convert_call_state with CONNECTING and unknown previous_state defaults to Trying. convert_call_media_state with NONE media_status returns None. RegistrationStateChanged with GetAccountInfo returning Err results in RegistrationFailed.

Edge case: pjsip_inv_state values outside 0-4 range return None from convert_call_state. AccountInfoSnapshot with registration_status=0 (unregistered) returns RegistrationFailed. call_id=0 and call_id=u64::MAX propagate correctly through conversions. RegistrationStarted acc_id=0 (sentinel) constructs correctly.

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] NativeEvent must be converted deterministically — same event always produces same SipEventPayload. pjsip_inv_state must be in range 0-4 before pattern matching. CONNECTING discrimination requires previous_state parameter.
- [Error invariant] On any unrecognized NativeEvent variant or out-of-range pjsip_inv_state value, the function returns None rather than panicking. GetAccountInfo error never produces a registration success event. Empty/zero-length digit in DtmfDigit never panics.
- [Internal state invariant] convert_call_state is stateless (pure function) — all state needed for CONNECTING discrimination is passed via previous_state parameter. convert_call_media_state takes backend reference for media_status query — no mutable state held across calls.
- [Boundary invariant] pjsip_inv_state values 0 and 5+ must both return None (distinct boundary behavior at both ends). call_id=0 and call_id=u64::MAX must propagate unchanged. AccountInfoSnapshot.registration_expires=0 maps to RegistrationFailed.
tickets.instrumentation:
- [Logging] Use tracing::debug!(target: "siprs::state", native_event = ?event_variant, call_id = ?call_id, "NativeEvent converted to SipEventPayload") at info level for successful conversions. Use tracing::warn! for unexpected/out-of-range pjsip_inv_state values. No per-digit logging for DtmfDigit to avoid log spam.
- [Metrics] No metrics in this layer — the conversion is stateless and zero-cost. Downstream consumers (Reactor, EventBus) add latency/gap metrics.
- [Error tracking] Out-of-range pjsip_inv_state values (>4) log a warning with the raw value. GetAccountInfo errors from AccountInfoSnapshot conversion log at error level with account_id context.
- [Health check] No health check in conversion layer. Health is verified by publishing a test NativeEvent and asserting the correct SipEventPayload arrives on EventBus (integration test).

(3) Implement convert_call_state + convert_call_media_state in m20_callstate_mapping.rs. (4) Create AccountInfoSnapshot struct + registration_state_to_event in m20_registr_cmd_pat.rs. (5) Create src/state/mod.rs with sub-module declarations. (6) Add pub mod state; to lib.rs. (7) Write tests (RED phase) before each implementation step.
- [Risks] CONNECTING discrimination requires previous_state from CallEntry — this state must be passed from the caller (Reactor) which may not yet implement call tracking. Consider making previous_state optional (Option<CallState>) with default to Trying. AccountInfoSnapshot uses pjsip_status_code (u16) — ensure the 200-vs-other comparison is robust against non-standard codes (183, 100, etc.).
- [Caveats] NativeEvent enum must be #[non_exhaustive] for forward compatibility. The conversion function signature takes &dyn SipBackend for media_status queries — the backend must not panic when queried for a non-existent call. DtmfDigit digit field must accept char (single character per PJSIP spec).
- [Open items] P2 NativeEvent variants (CallTsxStateChanged, etc.) return None for now — confirm with integration tests that these events are indeed produced by PJSIP callbacks and should be ignored at the conversion layer rather than filtered earlier. EventBus publish error handling (RecvError::Lagged) is left to Reactor.

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Translatability improvements for P1-2 implementation:

1. Function naming (verb phrases): convert_native_event_to_payload, convert_call_state, convert_call_media_state, registration_state_to_event — all read as explicit actions. No abbreviations or acronyms beyond standard ones.

2. Variable naming (domain concepts): Use previous_call_state not prev; registration_status not rs; native_event not ev. AccountInfoSnapshot field names match RFC prose: registration_status, registration_expires, online_status.

3. One function, one responsibility: convert_native_event_to_payload dispatches by variant to dedicated functions (convert_call_state, convert_call_media_state). No monolithic match-within-match logic. CONNECTING discrimination logic is self-contained in convert_call_state.

4. Hardcoded values as named constants: PJSIP_INV_STATE_NULL=0 through PJSIP_INV_STATE_DISCONNECTED=4 as named constants. MEDIA_STATUS_ACTIVE=0 through MEDIA_STATUS_ERROR=4 as named constants. Avoid raw integer literals in match patterns.

5. No error swallowing: All match arms return explicit values — no wildcard _ that silently ignores unexpected values. Out-of-range values log via tracing::warn! before returning None.

6. Existing code cleanup (Boy Scout): The placeholder pub enum State {} in all three files will be replaced with real implementations. The TODO: STUB comments will be removed. The src/state/mod.rs file (currently non-existent) will be created to properly declare module structure — this follows the Rust module file responsibility pattern (mod.rs = declarations only, no logic).

tickets.title: M20 DtmfSentInfo Two-Phase Design
tickets.background:
- Goal: Implement DtmfSentInfo struct, SentDtmfError enum, and establish the two-phase DTMF send semantics (immediate command accept + async DtmfSent event) in src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs
- Purpose: SipClient::send_dtmf() callers need a way to distinguish command-queued (synchronous return) from actual DTMF-sent or failed (asynchronous DtmfSent event). Without two-phase design, callers cannot tell whether DTMF digits were really sent or merely queued.
- Motivation: P0 priority per M20 implementation map. Required by zasso voice communication for reliable DTMF feedback during calls. The 500ms timeout fallback ensures no event is lost even if PJSIP callback is unavailable.
- Constraints: No FFI bindings exist yet (pjsua_call_dial_dtmf not accessible from Rust). SentDtmfError uses simulated pj_status_t (PJ_EINVALIDOP_SIM pattern). SipEventPayload::DtmfSent variant is not yet added (deferred to P5-1). Must be self-contained in single file following P1-2 pattern.
scope: src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs — DtmfSentInfo struct and SentDtmfError enum
DtmfSentInfo: method, digit, status: Result<(), SentDtmfError>, pjsip_status
SentDtmfError: PjsipError(pj_status_t), Timeout
Two-phase semantics: send_dtmf() return = command accepted, DtmfSent event = actual send/fallback
src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs — ADD — DtmfSentInfo struct, SentDtmfError enum, two-phase docs, and #[cfg(test)] test module
Convert empty `pub trait Service {}` stub to real struct/enum/pub(crate) API -- Before: just STUB marker, After: DtmfSentInfo struct + SentDtmfError enum + comprehensive tests
API contract: Add pub(crate) DtmfSentInfo + pub(crate) SentDtmfError — internal API for reactor/facade layers to construct and consume DTMF send results
No schema change — DtmfSentInfo uses existing types (DtmfMethod from command_serialization, Result from std)
No config change — timeout constant is compile-time (DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS). DtmfConfig deferred to P0-7.
No new dependencies — all types (Result, Option, char, i32) are std-only. Uses existing crate:: paths.
PJSIP FFI backend integration (pjsua_call_dial_dtmf) — deferred to P0-5 reactor layer for real backend wiring
FFI integration requires actual PJSUA instance + bindgen bindings which are not available in this crate phase. The struct and two-phase logic are platform-agnostic.
RuntimeCommand::SendDtmf handler (runtime/reactor.rs) — DtmfSent event emission will need a timer-based fallback in the reactor
DtmfSent event reaches the reactor's event processing pipeline — the new DtmfSentInfo struct is consumed by async DtmfSent event emission, but no API surface change (SipEventPayload not yet updated)
Yes — P0-5 reactor layer must implement timer spawning for 500ms fallback and wire DtmfSentInfo into SipEventPayload::DtmfSent

# Investigation Evidence for P1-3

## RFC Design (RFC-ROOT.md §20)
- DtmfSentInfo struct defined with fields: method:DtmfMethod, digit:char, status:Result<(), SentDtmfError>, pjsip_status:Option<pj_status_t>
- SentDtmfError enum: PjsipError(pj_status_t), Timeout
- Two-phase design: send_dtmf() returns Ok(()) immediately (command accepted by Reactor), DtmfSent event fires async when PJSIP actually sends or timeout occurs
- Priority Q2:A: DTMF two-phase (return value=command accepted, DtmfSent=send complete)
- Priority Q14:A: DtmfSent: PJSIP callback absent => 500ms timeout fallback
- 500ms default timeout via DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms

## Target Implementation File
- src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs (N0029) — currently empty STUB with `pub trait Service {}`
- No mod.rs in api/ — lib.rs does not declare `pub mod api` — requires module resolution during implementation

## Existing Pattern (P1-2 m20_registr_cmd_pat.rs)
- Same crate location pattern: struct definition + conversion function + #[cfg(test)] tests
- AccountInfoSnapshot struct mirrors what DtmfSentInfo needs: data struct with typed fields
- registration_state_to_event() conversion function pattern
- Tests: precondition (constructable), postcondition (variant dispatch), invariant (determinism, traits)

## Existing Infrastructure
- RuntimeCommand::SendDtmf variant exists in command_serialization.rs with call_id/digits/method/reply
- DtmfMethod stub: Rfc2833, Info, Inband (3 variants matching PJSUA_*_METHOD values)
- SipErrorKind::DtmfFailed and SipErrorKind::Timeout exist in error_design_siperror.rs
- SipReply<T> = oneshot::Sender<Result<T, SipError>> type alias exists
- CallId/AccountId newtypes exist in command_serialization.rs
- NativeEvent::DtmfDigit variant exists in m20_native_event_conv.rs
- Minimal SipEventPayload has DtmfReceived but NOT DtmfSent

## Pattern Reference (m20_runtime_command_error.rs)
- Error conversion pattern: PJ_EINVALIDOP_SIM = -15000 constant
- convert_conf_connect_error / convert_get_account_info_error functions map pj_status->SipError
- Same pattern applies to SentDtmfError::PjsipError conversion

## PJSIP Reference (vendor/pjsip)
- pjsua_call_dial_dtmf(call_id, digits) — RFC2833 only
- pjsua_call_dial_dtmf2(call_id, digits, duration)
- pjsua_call_send_dtmf(call_id, param) — full method control
- on_dtmf_digit, on_dtmf_digit2, on_dtmf_event callbacks
- No Rust FFI bindings exist yet

## Key Decision Points
- Module location: src/api/ has no mod.rs — may need to relocate or create module infrastructure
- DtmfMethod origin: currently in command_serialization.rs as stub — may move to api/ with canonical definition
